reviews.title: Dire beyond belief
reviews.text:
Epson you have yet again exceeded my expectations…

I fully expected this app to be bad - unintuitive, melon-twistingly frustrating even. Somehow though, your incredible product teams have managed to engineer out of this app, and the printer that I’m vainly attempting to access, any vestige of usability, functionality or in fact - point in it even existing.

To access the printer using the Epson iPrint app, I simply have to:
1. select the connected printer, verify that it cannot be communicated with for printing
2. perform a full factory reset
3. hold down a series of buttons to enable a new direct connection to a mobile phone (I’d really like to print from my WiFi connected laptop, but I assume this must only be available via an Epson EasiPrint subscription)
4. hold down more buttons to print four sheets of paper that hide details of a secret WiFi connection to the printer (and don’t think you can skip this step by doing something potentially IP-infringing like ‘writing down the details for next time…’ Epson’s customer experience team saw you coming a mile off buddy.
5. connect to the direct printer WiFi connection (and you can forget about Internet access from your phone now too - you don’t need anything that could distract you from your print job)
6. Select the document you want to print (better hope you didn’t forget to download it to your phone, or it’s back to step 1 you go my friend). Also, if it’s not a pdf document, then you’ll need to translate that thing like it’s
